coverageNote: Topic-level, paraphrased, non-authoritative. Compiled via a research fan-out across all 19 HITRUST assessment domains, serialized into 6 smaller domain groups (rather than one 19-domain fan-out) to bound per-run agent spend, followed within each group by a dedupe/reconcile pass and a dual-pass adversarial verification (checking citation resolution, tier/baseline-overlap attribution, and precision-overclaiming) before anything shipped -- see this plugin's hitrust-controls-compiler skill for the process. This compile's honest, cited count is 92 topic-level entries -- well short of the ~187 individual MyCSF requirement-statement count publicly cited for i1, because that figure counts requirement statements while this pipeline (by design, to stay public and non-authoritative) produces topic-level entries that each bundle multiple requirements; closing that gap fully would require the licensed MyCSF export this file deliberately does not use. Three domains (Password Management, Access Control, Incident Management) came back thin from a first pass leaning on scarce/weak sources and got a second, targeted research pass specifically to find better citations before shipping -- Incident Management grew from 2 to 7 entries this way, Access Control 3 to 4, Password Management 2 to 4; other domains were not re-run and reflect a single pass. 4 entries were recovered from this compile's own verification rejections after review found they were rejected ONLY for duplicating an entry in this exact file's own prior version (being wholesale-replaced by this compile, not merged with it) -- every other check on those 4 had passed; one of the four (an Access Control/Physical-security-adjacent visitor-tracking entry) had its baselineOverlap value corrected from 'false' to 'unsure' per the rejecting verifier's own more cautious note. 13 of 92 entries (14%) carry a citation-verified relatedControlCode; the rest ship as domain/topic-only, per this compile's opportunistic-citation discipline (a code is only ever included when a fetched public source verifies it for that specific topic, never invented) -- two additional codes a research agent proposed were dropped entirely during assembly for not matching a clean, verifiable crosswalk-code format (one was a legacy CSF 10.0-scheme reference incompatible with current v11 domain numbering, the other a raw MyCSF Unique-ID fragment rather than a control-reference code). Citations lean on a mix of official HITRUST Alliance pages, HITRUST-authorized-assessor firm write-ups, and independent secondary analyses (including one recurring author's HITRUST i1 breakdown series on LinkedIn for a large share of entries) -- none of it is MyCSF-derived or verbatim. Treat this as a starting map for planning, not ground truth: consult MyCSF or an authorized HITRUST assessor for exact requirement statement text, control codes, and counts before relying on it for a real assessment.

controls.topicLabel: Information Security Policy
controls.topicSummary: A documented information security policy (or policy set) that is approved by management, communicated to staff, and kept current through periodic review and revision. Same core artifact required at e1, but i1 expects fuller, more specific coverage of every evaluative element tested.

controls.topicLabel: Information Protection Program Governance & Continuous Improvement
controls.topicSummary: A formally established information protection program with defined ownership and objectives, run as a living program with a build-check-improve cadence rather than a static, annually-signed document.

controls.topicLabel: Personnel Screening and Disciplinary Handling
controls.topicSummary: Appropriate vetting of personnel before granting access to information assets, paired with a defined, consistently applied process for addressing policy violations from corrective feedback up to formal discipline.

controls.topicLabel: Comprehensive Anti-Malware/Anti-Spyware Coverage Across All Endpoints
controls.topicSummary: Anti-malware/anti-spyware tooling installed, current, and actively updated across essentially every device type touching the network (including BYOD), scanning across email, web, and inserted media, with a compensating network-level control where endpoint agents can't run.

controls.topicLabel: Compensating Controls for Unknown/Zero-Day Malware Threats
controls.topicSummary: Supplementary protections beyond signature-based anti-malware, such as heuristic/behavior-based detection and file-integrity monitoring, plus built-in OS security features, to catch threats signatures would miss.

controls.topicLabel: Endpoint- and Server-Level Anti-Spam/Suspicious Email Blocking
controls.topicSummary: Filtering of spam/phishing content and blocking of risky attachments or file types at both the network/server perimeter and the endpoint, layering endpoint-side scanning on top of gateway filtering.

controls.topicLabel: Host-Based Endpoint Firewall with Default-Deny Posture
controls.topicSummary: Host-based firewalls on endpoints configured to default-deny, permitting only explicitly approved inbound/outbound traffic; noted as relocated into this domain in the newer CSF version.

controls.topicLabel: Unattended Equipment Protection (Screensaver / Session Lockout)
controls.topicSummary: Protection of unattended workstations/devices via automatic screensaver activation and session lockout after inactivity, reducing risk of misuse of an unlocked endpoint.

controls.topicLabel: Restricting User-Level Software Installation on Endpoints
controls.topicSummary: A technical control governing end users' ability to install software on their own endpoints, aimed at preventing unauthorized or unvetted applications, distinct from application-whitelisting and awareness-training controls elsewhere.

controls.topicLabel: Technical Enforcement of Media Restrictions (Endpoint Hardening)
controls.topicSummary: Where portable media isn't authorized, technical/endpoint-level blocking (e.g., disabling ports or device classes) is expected rather than relying on written policy alone.

controls.topicLabel: Encryption of Sensitive Data on Digital Portable Media
controls.topicSummary: Sensitive information stored on digital removable media is expected to be encrypted, protecting it from unauthorized access if the media is lost or stolen.

controls.topicLabel: Anti-Malware Scanning of Removable Media Before Use
controls.topicSummary: Removable media is scanned for malware prior to connection to or use on organizational systems, to prevent malware introduction via USB or similar devices.

controls.topicLabel: Physical Transit Protection & Accountability (Digital vs. Non-Digital Media)
controls.topicSummary: Sensitive data moved off-site (e.g., backup tapes, shipped equipment) requires accountability and tracking during transport; digital media additionally requires encryption, while non-digital (paper) media requires accountability without an encryption expectation.

controls.topicLabel: Business-Justified Restriction on Portable Media Use
controls.topicSummary: Use of removable/portable storage devices (USB drives, external disks, optical media, backup tapes) is limited to situations with a documented legitimate business need rather than open use.

controls.topicLabel: Mobile Device Inventory & Authorized Connection Management
controls.topicSummary: A formal inventory of mobile devices that connect to or access organizational systems/data, with control over which devices may connect; i1 reportedly dropped case-by-case connection authorization in favor of a documented device inventory.

controls.topicLabel: Prevention of Rooted/Jailbroken Devices (Device Integrity)
controls.topicSummary: Controls to detect or prevent rooted/jailbroken mobile devices from accessing organizational data, since such devices have bypassed built-in OS security protections and are more vulnerable to malware.

controls.topicLabel: Teleworking / Remote Access Session & Physical Controls
controls.topicSummary: For remote employees, session/idle timeout limits, automatic screen locks, and privacy screens to reduce shoulder-surfing and unauthorized viewing of sensitive data outside the office; tests both logical and physical controls.

controls.topicLabel: Mobile Device Security for High-Risk Travel
controls.topicSummary: Mobile device configuration and integrity verification specifically for personnel traveling to higher-risk regions/countries, reflecting elevated exposure to tampering, surveillance, or seizure risk.

controls.topicLabel: Wireless Network Authorization & Encryption
controls.topicSummary: Wireless access points and client connections must be formally approved before use and must apply strong encryption (at minimum modern WPA2/AES-class protection, moving toward stronger cryptography) for both authentication and data transmission over the wireless network.

controls.topicLabel: Wireless Access Point Physical Placement & Tamper Prevention
controls.topicSummary: Access points should be sited in locations that limit physical access and tampering risk, as part of formally approving where and how wireless infrastructure is deployed.

controls.topicLabel: Unauthorized/Rogue Wireless Access Point Detection
controls.topicSummary: Organizations must periodically scan for and identify unauthorized or rogue wireless access points and networks operating in or near their facilities, a requirement treated as relevant even for organizations that do not intentionally deploy wireless infrastructure.

controls.topicLabel: Disabling Unused Wireless Capability on Devices
controls.topicSummary: Devices and equipment (such as printers or other peripherals) that have no legitimate business need for wireless connectivity should have their wireless radios or capabilities disabled to reduce the attack surface.

controls.topicLabel: Baseline Compliance Assessment & Configuration Drift Monitoring
controls.topicSummary: Beyond simply setting a baseline, the domain expects ongoing verification that live systems still match the approved configuration baseline, with configuration changes flowing only through the approved change process; secondary guidance for cloud environments frames this as automated drift detection against an infrastructure-as-code baseline.

controls.topicLabel: Formal Change Management Process for Production Systems
controls.topicSummary: The domain requires a controlled, auditable change management process for changes to production systems and configurations, covering formal change documentation, testing/quality checks, authorization and approval before implementation, and the ability to roll back a change, with an emphasis on evidence that these steps are actually executed rather than just documented in policy.

controls.topicLabel: Supply Chain Protections for Software/Configuration Changes
controls.topicSummary: The domain now includes supply-chain-oriented protections as part of configuration management, reflecting concern over the integrity of software and components introduced into the environment through vendors, build pipelines, or third-party code as changes are deployed.

controls.topicLabel: Tiered Deployment Structures (Environment Separation)
controls.topicSummary: The redesigned domain calls for organizations to maintain tiered deployment structures -- separated development, test, and production environments -- so that changes progress through controlled stages before reaching production.

controls.topicLabel: Comprehensive, Continuously-Validated Technology Asset & Software Inventory
controls.topicSummary: The dominant focus of the domain: organizations must build and keep current a wide-reaching inventory covering essentially every technology asset and data repository in the environment (servers, endpoints, network gear, cloud instances, containers, IoT, SANs, and portable/mobile devices), with the inventory periodically checked or validated rather than treated as a one-time exercise. This inventory is also expected to capture installed software/technology components so it can feed baseline and change-control decisions in the adjacent Configuration Management domain. Public assessor commentary notes the asset-inventory theme alone accounts for roughly five of the domain's twelve requirements and the large majority of its scored evaluative elements, making it by far the domain's biggest single emphasis in HITRUST CSF v11-based i1 assessments.

controls.topicLabel: Vulnerability Identification & Timely Remediation Program
controls.topicSummary: Beyond scanning alone, the domain expects a running program that tracks vulnerability-relevant details (software vendor, version, deployment status, and the internal owner responsible) for both infrastructure/endpoint systems and applications, and drives timely remediation action once a technical vulnerability is identified, using automation where practical. A legacy HITRUST CSF control reference for this theme appears in third-party compliance-mapping documentation under the older CSF 10.0 numbering scheme, which differs from the current v11-based domain numbering.

controls.topicLabel: Recurring Vulnerability Scanning Coverage Across the Full Asset Inventory
controls.topicSummary: The domain anchors on ongoing, recurring vulnerability scanning that covers the complete asset inventory rather than a one-time or point-in-time check, with cadence expectations tied to how the environment is scoped. One assessor's public v11 breakdown notes a prior requirement to run periodic penetration tests may have been dropped in favor of this general scanning expectation, though other secondary sources describe i1 as still including scanning plus periodic penetration testing, so that detail should be treated as unsettled rather than confirmed.

controls.topicLabel: Network Segmentation, Perimeter Gateways & Controlled Interconnections
controls.topicSummary: Requires the network to be designed into distinct security zones separated by dedicated perimeter gateway devices (e.g., firewalls) that validate source and destination addresses at internal and external control points, restrict traffic to explicitly authorized paths between zones, and ensure that any third-party or vendor connectivity into the network is routed through monitored, session-based access rather than direct, unmediated connections.

controls.topicLabel: Default-Deny Egress Filtering & Malicious-Domain/IP Blocking
controls.topicSummary: Requires outbound network traffic to be filtered under a default-deny posture, with reputation-based blocking of known malicious IP addresses and domains (commonly enforced at the DNS layer) so that internal assets cannot reach disallowed or known-bad destinations on the internet.

controls.topicLabel: Network-Based Intrusion Detection/Prevention & Threat-Intelligence Blocking
controls.topicSummary: Requires network-layer detection and prevention capability that inspects traffic for known attack signatures, command-and-control communication, and other indicators of compromise, and that automatically blocks or alerts on matches using regularly updated threat-intelligence feeds.

controls.topicLabel: Documented Port & Protocol Authorization
controls.topicSummary: Requires organizations to maintain a documented, justified inventory of which network ports, protocols, and services are permitted at each network boundary, along with a mechanism to detect and flag any live configuration that deviates from the approved list.

controls.topicLabel: Contractual Right-to-Audit for Network Service Providers
controls.topicSummary: Requires that agreements with third-party network or telecommunications service providers include contractual clauses granting the organization (or its assessor) the right to audit the provider's security practices as they affect the organization's network environment.

controls.topicLabel: Cryptographic Key Management
controls.topicSummary: Covers governance over the lifecycle of encryption keys used to protect transmitted data, including how keys are generated, stored, rotated on a defined schedule, and access-restricted (e.g., via role-based access and strong authentication for key administrators). Framed as a distinct concern layered on top of encryption protocol selection within the domain.

controls.topicLabel: Email Perimeter Content and Attachment Filtering
controls.topicSummary: Requires blocking or quarantining suspicious inbound email at the network perimeter and filtering out risky or unnecessary attachment/file types before they reach end users, as a server-side control distinct from endpoint-level malware protection.

controls.topicLabel: Email Domain Authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)
controls.topicSummary: Requires organizations to implement sender-authentication mechanisms for their email domains -- SPF, DKIM, and DMARC -- to reduce spoofing and phishing risk; in the v11 revision this requirement's scope was expanded from SPF alone to also explicitly include DKIM and DMARC.

controls.topicLabel: System Interconnection & Electronic Commerce Agreements
controls.topicSummary: Requires formal, documented agreements between organizations whenever system interconnections exist or network-based services are provided to one another, including specific arrangements covering electronic-commerce style data exchange; can be marked not-applicable when no such interconnections or electronic commerce functions exist.

controls.topicLabel: User Identity Verification Prior to Password Reset
controls.topicSummary: A distinct i1-level expectation that help desks or self-service reset mechanisms verify a requester's identity before issuing or resetting a password, to prevent social-engineering-based account takeover.

controls.topicLabel: Secure Password Communication Methods
controls.topicSummary: Initial or reset passwords/credentials should be delivered to users through channels that protect them from interception or exposure, rather than sent in the clear (e.g., plain email); called out as its own coverage area distinct from general policy enforcement.

controls.topicLabel: Baseline User Password Management (Policy, Secure Storage, No Sharing/Reuse, Quality Selection)
controls.topicSummary: Carried forward from earlier CSF versions, this core requirement expects organizations to communicate password-policy expectations, keep passwords stored securely rather than written on unsecured notes, prohibit account/password sharing and reuse, and require a reasonably strong password choice, though HITRUST does not define a numeric strength/entropy bar.

controls.topicLabel: Technical Enforcement of Password Policy Controls
controls.topicSummary: Password-policy rules must be enforced through system/technical controls rather than relying on written policy or user behavior alone; described as a v11 change that broadened a rule formerly scoped only to mobile devices into a more general requirement.

controls.topicLabel: Session and Connection Time Limitation
controls.topicSummary: Controls that cap how long an authenticated session or connection may remain open or idle, shrinking the window in which an unattended session could be misused.

controls.topicLabel: Periodic Review of User Access Rights
controls.topicSummary: Regular re-validation that each user's granted permissions still match their current role, with entitlements no longer needed removed rather than left to accumulate.

controls.topicLabel: Multi-Factor Authentication for Remote, Privileged, and High-Risk Access
controls.topicSummary: Strong multi-factor authentication enforced for remote connections, administrative/privileged logins, and other high-risk access scenarios, favoring phishing-resistant factors over simple SMS codes.

controls.topicLabel: Access Provisioning, Unique Accounts & De-provisioning
controls.topicSummary: Requires a formal process to request, authorize, and communicate account access, assign each user a unique identifier, and promptly remove access on separation or role change; described as the enduring core of the domain even after v11 trimmed the overall requirement count.

controls.topicLabel: Audit Log Generation & Content Requirements
controls.topicSummary: Systems handling covered information must produce secure audit records showing who did what, when, and to which system or record - user identity, timestamps, action taken, and success/failure outcome - with enough contextual detail (source IP, device, application) to support later forensic reconstruction.

controls.topicLabel: Centralized Log Aggregation & SIEM / Cross-Environment Monitoring
controls.topicSummary: Feeding logs from across the environment (operating systems, applications, network/security devices, wireless, IDS/IPS, anti-malware, cloud services) into a centralized SIEM or log-analytics platform to enable correlation and analysis across systems rather than isolated per-system review.

controls.topicLabel: Protection, Restricted Access & Tamper-Resistance of Audit Logs
controls.topicSummary: Safeguarding audit logs and the tools used to access them from unauthorized viewing, modification, or deletion - e.g., via file-integrity/change-detection monitoring or immutable, write-once storage - so log data can be trusted as evidence after the fact.

controls.topicLabel: Administrator & Privileged-User Activity Logging
controls.topicSummary: High-privilege actions - use of root/admin accounts, security configuration changes, other administrator/operator activity - must be logged distinctly, so privileged actions are traceable separately from ordinary user activity.

controls.topicLabel: System Fault / Error Logging
controls.topicSummary: System faults and errors need to be logged and reviewed, not just security-relevant user actions, so operational failures that could indicate or mask a security issue are captured and analyzed.

controls.topicLabel: Time Synchronization Across Systems
controls.topicSummary: Clocks across all in-scope systems must be synchronized to a reliable time source (a tight tolerance against UTC is described) so timestamps in logs from different systems can be accurately correlated during an investigation.

controls.topicLabel: Periodic Physical Access Log Review
controls.topicSummary: Logs of physical entry to facilities or sensitive areas are expected to be reviewed on a regular (e.g., weekly) cadence as part of the broader logging-and-monitoring program, not just generated and stored.

controls.topicLabel: Onboarding & Annual Security Awareness Training (Expanded, Role-Tailored)
controls.topicSummary: Carries forward the baseline new-hire and annual security-awareness training requirement but expands it with prescriptive content criteria and role-tailored tracks for security/privacy personnel, going beyond a generic training module.

controls.topicLabel: Rules of Behavior / Acceptable Use Policy Training
controls.topicSummary: Personnel must be trained on and acknowledge documented rules of behavior governing acceptable use of organizational systems and data, as a conduct-and-accountability control alongside general awareness training.

controls.topicLabel: Controlling Unauthorized Software Installation & Training Staff to Evaluate Software
controls.topicSummary: Personnel are trained on restrictions around installing software on endpoints and on evaluating whether software is safe or authorized before use, pairing a technical control with an education component.

controls.topicLabel: Secure Development / Secure Coding Training for Developers
controls.topicSummary: Developers receive specialized secure-coding training distinct from general staff awareness, reflecting a role-based training track for technical personnel.

controls.topicLabel: Third-Party Due Diligence Prior to Engagement
controls.topicSummary: Before onboarding a vendor or service provider with access to sensitive systems or data, the organization formally evaluates that third party's information security posture as part of selection, rather than accepting a new vendor on trust.

controls.topicLabel: Formal Third-Party Contracts and Security/Privacy Obligations (SLAs)
controls.topicSummary: Third-party relationships are governed by written agreements or SLAs that explicitly state the vendor's information security and privacy obligations, making expectations contractually enforceable.

controls.topicLabel: Third-Party Personnel Screening and Security-Training Flow-Down
controls.topicSummary: Personnel-security expectations extend to vendors, so a third party's own staff who touch organizational information are subject to appropriate background screening and security/privacy training obligations.

controls.topicLabel: Periodic Reassessment / Ongoing Monitoring of Third-Party Security
controls.topicSummary: Vendor security is periodically reassessed and documented (e.g., on an annual cycle) for the life of the relationship rather than checked only at onboarding.

controls.topicLabel: Documented Acknowledgment of Third-Party Security Responsibilities
controls.topicSummary: Third parties formally acknowledge in writing that they understand and accept their information security responsibilities and liabilities before being granted access to organizational information assets.

controls.topicLabel: Third-Party Inherent-Risk Tiering / Classification
controls.topicSummary: Organizations classify each third party's inherent risk (data sensitivity/volume, relationship criticality, remote-access model) so that due-diligence rigor scales with risk before deciding how much assurance to demand.

controls.topicLabel: Corrective Action Tracking for Third-Party Control Gaps
controls.topicSummary: When a vendor assessment surfaces control deficiencies, the organization obtains and tracks a documented corrective action plan (or approves a compensating control) with the third party until the gap is remediated.

controls.topicLabel: Formal, Documented Incident Response Plan
controls.topicSummary: A formally documented incident response plan lays out the organization's overall approach for detecting, responding to, and managing security incidents.

controls.topicLabel: Evidence Collection & Retention for Investigations
controls.topicSummary: The domain includes requirements around properly collecting, preserving, and retaining evidence generated during an incident so it can support internal investigations and potential legal or regulatory proceedings.

controls.topicLabel: Incident Detection and Alerting
controls.topicSummary: Organizations must run continuous monitoring and alerting (e.g., anomaly/threat detection feeding a security operations workflow) so incidents are identified near real-time rather than discovered after the fact.

controls.topicLabel: Incident Containment Capability
controls.topicSummary: i1 expects pre-defined, executable containment actions (e.g., isolating a compromised system, revoking credentials, blocking malicious traffic) that can be applied quickly once an incident is confirmed.

controls.topicLabel: Incident Eradication and Recovery
controls.topicSummary: Beyond containment, i1 looks for a defined approach to removing an incident's root cause (e.g., rebuilding from a known-good baseline) and restoring affected systems and data using established recovery points.

controls.topicLabel: Incident Response Plan Testing (Tabletop/Exercises)
controls.topicSummary: The incident response plan must be periodically tested through structured exercises involving actual responders, with results and gaps documented as evidence the plan works in practice and not only on paper.

controls.topicLabel: Post-Incident Review, Metrics, and Continuous Improvement
controls.topicSummary: After an incident, i1 expects a root-cause review that feeds lessons learned back into the response plan, along with tracking operational metrics such as time-to-detect, time-to-contain, and time-to-recover as evidence of program maturity.

controls.topicLabel: Business Impact Analysis & Critical Process Identification
controls.topicSummary: Formally identifies which business processes, applications, and data are critical to operations and estimates the operational impact of their disruption, setting scope and priorities for the rest of continuity planning.

controls.topicLabel: Business Continuity Governance Framework
controls.topicSummary: Establishes an organization-wide business continuity planning framework defining structure, ownership, and scope for continuity activities across the enterprise, distinct from any single plan document.

controls.topicLabel: Alternate Processing & Storage Site Arrangements
controls.topicSummary: Arranges alternate facilities, processing locations, or telecommunications capacity so critical operations and data recovery can continue if a primary site or system becomes unavailable.

controls.topicLabel: Backup Data Storage, Retention & Restoration Testing
controls.topicSummary: Maintains backup copies of systems and data in tracked, appropriately located storage, retains them per policy, and periodically tests that they can actually be restored.

controls.topicLabel: Offline / Immutable Data Backup Copies
controls.topicSummary: Maintains at least one backup copy that is offline or immutable so a clean, unalterable restore point survives even if production systems and connected backups are compromised (e.g. by ransomware).

controls.topicLabel: Contingency/BC-DR Personnel Training
controls.topicSummary: Trains staff who have continuity or disaster-recovery responsibilities on their specific roles so they can execute the plan effectively during an actual disruptive event.

controls.topicLabel: BC/DR Plan Testing, Exercises & Maintenance
controls.topicSummary: Periodically tests and exercises business continuity and disaster recovery plans (e.g. tabletop exercises or drills) and updates/reassesses plans based on results, organizational changes, or newly identified risks.

controls.topicLabel: Risk Consideration Embedded in Change Management
controls.topicSummary: Builds risk-impact analysis into the change management workflow so proposed system or process changes are evaluated for new or altered risk before approval and implementation.

controls.topicLabel: Layered Control Strategy in System Design
controls.topicSummary: Expects deliberate mixing of control types (preventive, detective, corrective, compensating) when building or changing systems, rather than relying on a single control type, to achieve defense in depth.

controls.topicLabel: Threat Intelligence and Situational Awareness
controls.topicSummary: Expects organizations to draw on external threat sources (feeds, information-sharing communities/ISACs, ongoing training) to keep risk assessments current with the evolving threat landscape rather than relying solely on internal data.

controls.topicLabel: Risk Treatment and Mitigation Planning
controls.topicSummary: Once risks are identified, expects the organization to define and carry out mitigation strategies to bring risk to an acceptable level, rather than stopping at identification and documentation alone.

controls.topicLabel: Risk Evaluation and Root-Cause Analysis
controls.topicSummary: Covers evaluating realized risks and incidents after the fact to understand underlying causes, feeding lessons learned back into the risk program so it improves over time.

controls.topicLabel: Power & Data Cabling Protection
controls.topicSummary: Physically shields power lines and data transmission cabling from damage, tampering, or unauthorized interception.

controls.topicLabel: Physical Asset Tracking & Equipment Siting
controls.topicSummary: Tracks the physical location and movement of IT equipment, and positions equipment to reduce exposure to environmentally hazardous or high-traffic areas.

controls.topicLabel: Secure Media and Equipment Disposal/Sanitization
controls.topicSummary: Encrypts data held on media and devices, sanitizes storage before reuse, and chooses destruction or disposal methods appropriate to data sensitivity when equipment is retired.

controls.topicLabel: Equipment Maintenance & Diagnostic Tool Controls
controls.topicSummary: Vets and supervises personnel who service or repair facility/IT equipment, and controls the diagnostic or maintenance tools they bring on-site or remove afterward.

controls.topicLabel: Visitor, Vendor & Maintenance-Personnel Access Tracking
controls.topicSummary: Logging and monitoring of physical access by maintenance providers, vendors, and other visitors -- capturing arrival, departure, and who authorized the visit -- as a distinct control from employee/contractor access management.

controls.topicLabel: Data & System Classification and Information Handling
controls.topicSummary: Calls for a documented data/system classification scheme (sensitivity or criticality tiers) and associated handling procedures so protective, risk-based controls are assigned and applied consistently across an asset or information item's lifecycle. Proposed independently under both Risk Management (framed around classification driving control selection) and Data Protection and Privacy (framed around a documented classification/handling scheme); merged here under the domain that most centrally owns classification.

controls.topicLabel: Records Retention, Minimization & Data Disposal
controls.topicSummary: Calls for a formal records retention and data-minimization program defining how long different data types are kept, flagging redundant or duplicate data for cleanup, and governing secure disposal once information is no longer needed for a business purpose.

controls.topicLabel: Privacy Policies, Notices & Privacy Impact Assessments
controls.topicSummary: Expects documented privacy policies and notices along with a process for assessing privacy risk (such as privacy impact assessments) connected to how personal information is collected, used, and disclosed.

controls.topicLabel: Data Loss Prevention & Sensitive Data Discovery
controls.topicSummary: Encourages capabilities to discover and inventory where regulated or sensitive data resides across the environment and to detect/prevent unauthorized exfiltration of that data.
